text:
mina: quick sync — I noticed our full benchmark reruns for every quantized/audio/tokenizer variant are killing onboarding throughput. proposal: shard-aware bench + golden-sample drift checks so we only rebench the delta sets. thoughts?

ben: +1 for avoiding full reruns. can you sketch the invariants we need to preserve across variants? latency percentile, sample-level token diffs?

sara: agreeing with ben. also need to capture subtle output drift — not just token-level diffs. e.g., reranking scores or classification probs. we should keep a lightweight semantic-similarity check.

mina: proposed invariants: 1) p50/p95 latency within X% of baseline for same hardware; 2) top-1 token agreement on golden inputs >= 98%; 3) for prob/class tasks, KL or JS divergence threshold; 4) no new OOM/crash traces. if shard-aware, bench only modified shards + a tiny sample from other shards to detect regressions.

alex: how do we pick the "tiny sample" to be representative? random may miss edge cases. recommend stratified picks by seq-len and prompt-type.

mina: good point. plan: stratify by seqlen buckets (0-64,65-256,256+), plus a handful of outlier prompts (rare tokens, long context). each shard defines bucket seeds.

ben: operationally, I think we can plugin a delta-driven runner in bench infra. naive sketch:
```
# pseudo
R = bench_registry.resolve(model_id)
deltas = diff(R.current_artifacts, R.candidate_artifacts)
shards_to_run = delta_shards(deltas)
rbench run --shards ${shards_to_run} --golden-sample-file shards/${id}/golden.json
```
This avoids touching identical shards.

mina: exactly. plus the golden-sample-file should contain per-shard stratified seeds. we can memoize interpreter-level seeds so quantized builds reuse same inputs.

sara: QA: how do we handle encoder-decoder models vs decoder-only when token alignment isn't comparable? e.g., seq2seq uses beam search and length differences.

ben: for seq2seq we'll compare normalized metrics: BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, and embed-sim for semantic checks. token-agreement is only for autoreg next-token tasks. separate comparator modules per architecture.

alex: CI integration: we must ensure PRs that change conversion scripts (quantization, onnx export) auto-trigger a delta bench plan. can we add a light gating job that runs the small stratified set and posts results to the PR?

ci-bot: patch #4821 triggered: changed exporter/quantize.py -> scheduled delta-bench with shards [2,7] and golden set. results will post within ~20m. :mag_right:

mina: nice. decision ideas so far: 1) implement delta-shard detection based on artifact fingerprinting (file-level + operator hash), 2) per-shard golden seeds and stratified tiny-sample, 3) comparator plugins per architecture (token-agree, embed-sim, prob-divergence, BLEU), 4) CI lightweight gate for PRs + full bench for release/major model changes.

sara: +1. add: monitor false-neg rate by logging when we promoted a variant that later failed full bench, so we can tune thresholds.

ben: tradeoffs: reduces cost but increases complexity and edge-case risk. recommend a gradual rollout: start with non-production models and a 24h shadow run where delta runner also queues full bench in background — compare decisions.

mina: agreed. rollout plan: stage 1 (2 weeks) run delta-shard & parallel full bench in background for newly onboarded models; collect metrics. stage 2: enable CI gate for non-prod; stage 3: enable for prod after thresholds stable.

alex: API/contract question: what does the bench adapter surface? I propose small JSON contract: {"model_id": "", "artifacts": [sha1...], "shards": [list], "golden_seeds": path, "comparators": ["token", "embed"]} — CI/registry can compute diffs and call runner.

mina: that matches my thinking. keep it flat simple. bench infra team can provide a CLI and a HTTP hook.

ci-bot: background full bench queued for model=redwood/experiment-5 id=rev-a1b2; will post results to #eng-ml when done.

sara: minor nit: ensure golden-seed storage is immutable per-artifact to avoid drift. put seeds under artifact-managed bucket + version.

ben: and add a cheap liveness smoke that runs the candidate binary for 1s with a warmup prompt to detect OOMs or assert failures before any benching.

mina: good call. I'll draft an RFC follow-up with: fingerprints spec, shard diff algorithm, comparator plugin interface, CI hook, rollout plan, and telemetry metrics to track (false-neg rate, %bench-cost saved, avg latency delta).

alex: timeline?

mina: draft by EOD Friday. @ben @sara please review early. I'll include example invocations and a small test harness.

ben: will review.

sara: same. thanks. :heart:

ci-bot: noted: reviewers assigned @ben @sara for RFC 2026-delta-bench.
